reviews.reason: Reviewed the full current proof and actual suppliers. Regularity implies unique components, so finitely many components are disjoint and clopen. Translations, inversion and conjugation prove the identity component is a normal irreducible subgroup with component cosets. Apply the same argument to the reduced classical stabilizer: its intersection with the identity component is a nonempty clopen union of equidimensional components, giving equal stabilizer dimensions. The connected orbit suppliers then apply with AC. Distinct connected-group orbits cannot meet one another's equal-dimensional closures, since that would force equal closures and intersecting dense opens. Their finite closed union gives the full orbit dimension and equidimensional closure; boundary connected orbits, and hence full orbits, have smaller dimension. Least nonnegative orbit dimension yields a closed orbit in every closure. Statement unchanged byte-for-byte.
